newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch railways 1996 net up 7 pct, below forecast.
newsitem.headline: Dutch railways 1996 net up 7 pct, below forecast.

text.p: State-owned Dutch Railways (Nederlandse Spoorwegen) on Friday reported a 1996 net profit of 105 million guilders, a rise of seven million guilders from 1995 which it said was below its previous expectations.
The seven percent profit rise resulted from lower financial charges and extraordinary results. The operating result, at 224 million guilders, was 26 million lower than in 1995.
The contraction came with disappointing figures for passenger and cargo transport and the group's railway construction subsidiary, it said in a statement.

The operating result of passenger division NS Reizigers fell by 52 million guilders to 79 million as higher revenue and cost reduction measures could not compensate for a 55 million guilder fall in the state subsidy.
Passenger kilometres rose to 14,131 million from 13,977 million in 1995.
The operating result of NS Cargo was an 18 million guilder loss, although this was better than than expected.
For NS Stations and NS Vastgoed, the property arm, the operating result was up 125 million guilders.
"Given a number of uncertainties and risks, it would not be appropriate to give a forecast of the profit expectation for 1997," the company said.
Dutch Railways has previously indicated it would like to float its shares, but this is unlikely to happen before 2002 when NS expects to be self-supporting.
